newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Cambodia's Ranariddh to shun ASEAN meeting.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Ranariddh to shun ASEAN meeting.

text.p: Ousted Cambodian first prime minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh does not plan to attend meetings of Southeast Asian nations and their allies this week, an official with his delegation said on Monday.

Ranariddh, whose forces were beaten this month in fighting with troops loyal to co-prime minister Hun Sen, had been expected to go to Kuala Lumpur for the annual meeting of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN).

"No, he won't be going there," the official said when asked if Ranariddh would attend. Cambodia had been scheduled to join the organisation during the meetings until ASEAN put its membership on hold because of the country's crisis.
"This is not a prime ministers' meeting. We need to meet with the prime ministers," she said.
"We are trying to get in touch with all ASEAN countries to arrange meetings officially," the official added.
The meeting of the ASEAN foreign ministers, at which Burma and Laos join the group, will be followed by a session of the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF).

That links ASEAN with the United States, the European Union, Japan, China, Russia, India and Australia. Diplomats said Ranariddh had been expected in the Malaysian capital to take advantage of the presence of so many countries. Instead, Ranariddh planned to return on Wednesday to Bangkok, where he met some ASEAN foreign ministers last week.
ASEAN now groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Hun Sen has rejected ASEAN efforts to find a solution to Cambodia's political crisis, which flared while Ranariddh was abroad.
It has sent people fleeing Phnom Penh and other areas of fighting and forced Thailand to brace for an influx of refugees.
On Monday, Ranariddh met Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong. Neither side offered details of the meeting.
